claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxygen resistance for high-temperature applications.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of approximately 1 at.% Al by vacuum arc melting.
Approximately 1 at.% Al will promote formation of an alumina scale on equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr during exposure to air at 800 °C.
The resulting alumina scale will be thin, continuous, and adherent.
Al has a strong affinity for oxygen.
Al promotes selective formation of thermodynamically stable Al2O3 during high-temperature oxidation.
A continuous alumina scale acts as a protective barrier that reduces oxygen penetration.
Reduced oxygen penetration will reduce oxidation-related degradation and pesting.
The approximately 1 at.% Al addition will preserve the underlying single-phase BCC microstructure.
The single-phase BCC microstructure governs the alloy's useful mechanical performance.
Relative to untreated material, the Al-modified alloy will show significantly lower mass gain or oxide-scale thickness after 5 hours in air at 800 °C.
The Al-modified alloy will retain room-temperature tensile ductility within or near the stated 8–16% range.
The Al-modified alloy will retain high-temperature yield strength within or near 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The proposed protective effect is limited to approximately 800 °C in air for approximately 5 hours.

contradictions.description: The conditions field implies that the 800 °C oxidation exposure occurs with mechanical loading consistent with both high-temperature yield and room-temperature ductility testing, whereas the experiment design specifies an unloaded oxidation exposure followed by separate mechanical tests.
